uncited: **Inputs:** A regular 3D grid of voxel data; a pre-computed min/max octree representing the volume; an orthogonal view direction.
**Outputs:** A 2D image where each pixel contains the accumulated color and opacity of the first opaque surface or the integrated transmittance along the ray.
**Min/Max Octree:** A hierarchical structure where each node stores the minimum and maximum scalar values of the voxels in its sub-volume.
**Hexagon Template:** A 2D mask representing the projection of a cubic sub-volume onto the image plane under orthogonal projection.
**Hierarchical Occlusion Maps (HOMs):** Images of varying resolutions used to track which rays have already been computed.
**Pre-computation:** Construct the min/max octree from the input volume data.
**Sub-volume Projection:** Divide the volume into sub-volumes of size $m^3$ voxels.
Project each sub-volume onto the image plane.
**Visibility Culling:** Use the min/max octree to determine if a sub-volume contains relevant data.
**Ray Traversal / Accumulation:** For visible sub-volumes, traverse the rays intersecting the hexagonal footprint.
*   For **isosurface rendering**: Check the hierarchical occlusion maps.
If the ray has already been computed (indicated by the HOM), reuse the previously computed value.
*   **Orthogonal Constraint:** The method relies on orthogonal projection to ensure the hexagonal footprint is constant.
